account: It is day 0, just after ten, and I am at the plaza for my scheduled market walk. Nothing unusual or alarming has been confirmed. Townsfolk 30 says there is no news; Townsfolk 10 and 20 are also nearby. The secretary has followed toward the plaza carrying a writable book, but I do not know why. Earlier the builder came to my office with a lantern, seeking an agreed repair scope and payment for this week's work, and said he had planks and lanterns ready. I know of no damaged sections yet, so I requested a proposed scope and price for my one o'clock accounts appointment and explicitly withheld authorization for paid work. This appears to be ordinary repair planning, not evidence of an emergency. The secretary offered to record an agreement. My afternoon tea appointment remains unclear: the book says only a neighbour's dockside cottage on the east bank, and the secretary does not know which neighbour or house. I heard the secretary and builder speaking as I left the office but could not understand their words. Today's remaining appointments are lunch at home at noon, accounts at one, tea at three, office at four-thirty, and home at seven.
